data.name: Kritavya
data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Sanskrit word ‘kri’ meaning to do and ‘tavya’ meaning bound or obligated. It signifies a person who is deeply committed to their duties and responsibilities.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Kritavya" signifies a strong sense of duty, honor, and responsibility within Hindu culture. The name carries an expectation of commitment to one's duties as well as to one's community and family. In this way, the name emphasizes the importance of taking action and living up to one's obligations.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Kritavya" can be seen as a reminder of the inner call to duty and service. It encourages introspection, self-reflection, and a deep commitment to living in alignment with one's dharma or purpose in life. The name also reflects the idea that every action we take, no matter how small, has an impact on the world around us and on our own spiritual growth. In this way, the name "Kritavya" inspires us to be mindful and purposeful in all that we do, and to use our actions as a means to bring positive change into the world.

historical_references.reference: Kritavya is mentioned in the Mahabharata as the name of a sage who was a disciple of Vyasa and the preceptor of the Pandava prince Bhima. He is also called Bhima-guru.
historical_references.context: ancient Indian epic poetry and mythology

historical_references.reference: Kritavya is also mentioned in the Puranic literature, particularly in the Mahabharata and the Bhagavad Purana, as a sage who performed a great penance to obtain the boon of immortality. He is also known as Kritavasa and Kritavarma.
